scenes.line1: How do generics keep Java safe?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how Java generics make your code safer, but also limit what you can do at runtime?

scenes.label: Generics
scenes.sub: Generics let you build type-safe collections.
scenes.say: Generics help you avoid runtime errors by enforcing type safety for collections and APIs.
Wildcards make APIs flexible. Use extends for reading, and super for writing to collections.

scenes.title: What happens at runtime?
scenes.say: At runtime, Java erases generic types. Both lists of strings and integers are just lists, so type checks are limited.

scenes.question: Can you check List<String> at runtime?
scenes.right: No. Type erasure means you can't check generic types like List of strings at runtime.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: You can't check for a list of strings at runtime, because type erasure removes that info.
